title_en: Venezuela opposition leader Machado returns after months in exile
title_zh: 委内瑞拉反对派领导人马查多在流亡数月后回归

paragraphs.en: CARACAS, Venezuela -- Opposition leader and Nobel laureate María Corina Machado reappeared in Venezuela Sunday for the first time since December, returning from exile at a time when doubts about the country's democratic future — and the role of the U.S. — are growing.
paragraphs.zh: 委内瑞拉加拉加斯——反对派领袖、诺贝尔奖得主玛丽亚·科里纳·马查多（María Corina Machado）周日在该国重新露面，这是她自去年12月以来的首次现身。她此番结束流亡回国之际，外界对委内瑞拉民主前景以及美国所扮演角色的疑虑正日益加深。

paragraphs.en: It was her first appearance since the U.S. military deposed the country’s then-President Nicolás Maduro in January, replacing him with an interim president who has exceeded the time she was authorized to serve , with no election scheduled.
paragraphs.zh: 这是自美国军方于今年1月推翻时任总统尼古拉斯·马杜罗（Nicolás Maduro）、以一位临时总统取而代之以来，她首次公开露面。这位临时总统的任职时间已超出其获准任职的期限，且没有安排选举。

paragraphs.en: “Today is a very important day for Venezuelans. Our sovereign voice returns with her to lead and guide this process!” he wrote. “You know it, this is until the end.”
paragraphs.zh: “今天对委内瑞拉人来说是极为重要的一天。我们主权的声音随她一同归来，来领导和指引这一进程！”他写道，“你知道的，这要坚持到底。”

paragraphs.en: On Sunday afternoon, Machado strode into a church in the state of Lara, west of Caracas, to the applause of dozens gathered there as they shook her hand and hugged her, with cellphones aloft to record her return.
paragraphs.zh: 周日下午，马查多大步走进加拉加斯以西拉腊州的一座教堂，聚集在那里的数十人报以掌声，与她握手、拥抱，并高举手机记录她的归来。

paragraphs.en: Asked by reporters Sunday about Machado’s return to Venezuela, U.S. President Donald Trump said, “I don’t know anything about it, but I think she’s a very nice woman. She gave me her Nobel Prize. So how can I say anything else? And I hope she’s safe. She’s a very nice woman. But we’re doing really well in Venezuela.”
paragraphs.zh: 周日，当记者问及马查多返回委内瑞拉一事时，美国总统唐纳德·特朗普表示：“我对此一无所知，但我认为她是一位非常好的女性。她把她的诺贝尔奖给了我。那我还能说什么呢？我希望她平安。她是一位非常好的女性。不过我们在委内瑞拉做得非常好。”

paragraphs.en: Machado was briefly detained in January 2025, following a protest against Maduro’s planned swearing-in ceremony, and went into hiding in Venezuela for 11 months. After making a clandestine escape from the country, she reappeared that December in Norway , where she was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize for her peaceful challenge to Maduro’s authoritarian government.
paragraphs.zh: 马查多于2025年1月在一次抗议马杜罗计划举行的宣誓就职仪式的活动后短暂被拘留，随后在委内瑞拉藏匿了11个月。在秘密逃离该国后，她于当年12月在挪威重新露面，并在那里获颁诺贝尔和平奖，以表彰她对马杜罗威权政府的和平挑战。

paragraphs.en: González took her place on the ballot, and ample credible evidence showed that he defeated Maduro by more than a 2-to-1 margin. But the National Electoral Council, which is stacked with ruling-party loyalists, declared Maduro the winner.
paragraphs.zh: 冈萨雷斯（González）代替她出现在选票上，大量可信证据表明他以超过二比一的优势击败了马杜罗。但由执政党忠实拥护者把持的全国选举委员会宣布马杜罗获胜。

paragraphs.en: The lead-up and aftermath of the election were marked by widespread government repression, including forced disappearances, torture and other human rights violations. More than 2,000 people, including poll workers, were detained in the days after the vote.
paragraphs.zh: 选举前前后后的过程充斥着政府的大范围镇压，包括强迫失踪、酷刑和其他侵犯人权行为。投票后的数日内，包括投票站工作人员在内的2000多人被拘留。

paragraphs.en: In January, the U.S. military captured Maduro in Caracas and whisked him to New York to face drug-related charges, which he has denied. Many Venezuelans were stunned by the Trump administration’s decision to work with Rodríguez, instead of Machado, to try to revitalize the crisis-racked country.
paragraphs.zh: 今年1月，美国军方在加拉加斯抓获马杜罗，并迅速将他送往纽约面对毒品相关指控，他对此予以否认。许多委内瑞拉人对特朗普政府决定与罗德里格斯（Rodríguez）而非马查多合作、试图重振这个危机缠身的国家感到震惊。
